refsection.title: Description
refsection.para: A Formation resource allows you to combine spacecraft in a “container” object and then GMAT’s propagation subsystem will model the collection of spacecraft as a coupled dynamic system. You can only propagate Formation resources using numerical-integrator type propagators. Configure individual formation fields before the Mission Sequence. A complete formation value can also be received through a GMAT function output; native field-edit restrictions remain in effect.

Target and Optimize iteration rollback can restore the captured member selection after a complete value changes it. Rollback uses the original live spacecraft and restores their captured values; an unrelated replacement object with the same name does not become a captured target. Propagation prepares its bindings again when member or state layouts change.

entry.para: Boolean; default false. Set true on every formation that will reference the same spacecraft. This permits shared definitions and copies that keep their spacecraft references. False retains exclusive membership. Configure this option before the mission sequence; it cannot be changed by a mission command. A single Propagate command still cannot include the same spacecraft more than once, including through different formations.
Adds a list of Spacecraft to the Formation. The list cannot be empty.

refsection.title: GUI
refsection.para: To create a simple Formation and configure its Spacecraft, in the Resource Tree:

listitem.para: Right-click the Spacecraft folder and select Add Spacecraft.
Right click the Formations folder and select Add Formation.
Double-click Formation1 to open its dialog box.
Click the right-arrow button twice to add DefaultSC and Spacecraft1 to Formation1.

note.para: With the default AllowSharedMembers=false, a Spacecraft can only be added to one Formation. Sharing requires AllowSharedMembers=true on every formation that uses the overlapping spacecraft.

refsection.title: Remarks
refsection.para: A Formation is a container object that allows you to model a group of Spacecraft as a coupled system. You can add Spacecraft to a Formation using the Add field as shown in the script examples below or in the GUI example above. The primary reasons to use a Formation Resource are (1) to simplify the propagation of multiple spacecraft and (2) for performance reasons. You can only add a spacecraft to only one formation by default. AllowSharedMembers=true explicitly permits shared spacecraft references; formations cannot contain other formations. GMAT’s propagation subsystem models Formations as a coupled dynamic system. Once spacecraft have been added to a Formation, you can easily propagate all of the spacecraft by simply including the formation in the Propagate command statement like this:

Native API membership edits invalidate the packed formation layout. Resolve all spacecraft references and call BuildState before using the edited layout. Members are packed in Add order; rebinding a same-name spacecraft replaces the old reference. State dimensions are recomputed from the resolved members, including after copying, removal, or clearing. A state update rejects incomplete layouts before modifying any spacecraft. Epoch consistency is checked again when building the state; members using precision time are also compared at their native precision. Propagation buffers without member bindings retain their copied state and epoch. Configured precision-time mode is preserved during state rebuilds. Normal propagation updates copy into the existing layout; rebuilding and resizing are reserved for changed layouts. The geometric-center state uses the first six Cartesian elements of each complete member-state packet.

A shared formation is another view of the same spacecraft, not a separate set of spacecraft. Its geometric-center state, Cartesian parameter values, and epoch queries read the current resolved members, including after another formation or an individual spacecraft has propagated or maneuvered. Native typed Cartesian and epoch setters update those same members. Changing a spacecraft through one view therefore affects every shared view. Member epochs must be synchronized before computing a coupled formation state.

To clone a populated formation while keeping its spacecraft references, enable AllowSharedMembers on the source and any other formations using those spacecraft, then use Clone in the Resource Tree. The copy inherits the option and the same Add list. Existing formations using exclusive membership continue to require disjoint members.

A native copy of a resolved shared formation captures current member state and epoch values even if the source's packed integration snapshot is older. A new clone has no member bindings until references are resolved; copying the object does not transfer ownership of its spacecraft.

Target and Optimize iteration snapshots also capture the actual spacecraft referenced by a formation. Rollback retains the current member bindings and restores compatible packed state storage. A member removed, replaced or rebound after capture requires native preparation before rollback, even if a replacement has the same name.

The native mutable GetState/GetPropItem accessors continue to expose packed integration storage. Native clients editing that storage refresh it with UpdateState before editing and commit Cartesian changes with UpdateElements; epoch changes use the epoch setters. Read-only shared state queries do not refresh or overwrite pending integration storage. Typed precision-epoch assignments retain GmatTime when updating the members.
You can only propagate Formation resources using numerical-integrator type propagators. GMAT does not support propagation of the orbit state transition matrix when propagating formations.
When propagating a Formation, all spacecraft in the Formation must have equivalent epochs. GMAT will allow you to separately propagate a Spacecraft that has been added to a Formation, like this:
However, when a Formation is propagated, if the epochs of all Spacecraft in the Formation are not equivalent to a tolerance of a few microseconds, GMAT will throw an error and execution will stop.

refsection.title: Setting Colors On Spacecrafts In Formation Resource
refsection.para: If you want to set unique colors on spacecraft trajectories that are nested in the Formation resource, then change colors through either the Spacecraft resource or the Propagate command. See the documentation for discussion and examples on how to set unique colors on Spacecraft resource and Propagate command.
